definitions.explanation: In geometry, a prism — a solid with two identical, parallel polygonal faces connected by rectangular faces. Also used outside math for square-cross-section pillars in buildings.

examples.japanese: {角柱|かくちゅう}の{体積|たいせき}を{求|もと}める。
examples.english: Find the volume of a prism.

examples.japanese: {三角柱|さんかくちゅう}には{底面|ていめん}が{二|ふた}つある。
examples.english: A triangular prism has two base faces.

examples.japanese: この{建物|たてもの}は{大|おお}きな{角柱|かくちゅう}で{支|ささ}えられている。
examples.english: This building is supported by large square pillars.

notes:
Compound of {角|かく} (corner; angle) + {柱|ちゅう} (pillar). The math meaning is the more common one in textbooks; the architectural meaning appears in construction contexts.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {三角柱|さんかくちゅう}: triangular prism
- {四角柱|しかくちゅう}: square prism (cuboid)
- {六角柱|ろっかくちゅう}: hexagonal prism

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {円柱|えんちゅう}: cylinder — round cross-section instead of polygonal
- {角錐|かくすい}: pyramid — comes to a single point instead of a parallel face
- {柱|はしら}: pillar (general, everyday word)
